chest-big.title: Chest line + big word
chest-big.use: A setup line plus one key word. The most-used layout — at least 3 per talking-head video.
chest-big.avoid: Three in a row turns into "everything is the point = nothing is the point".

strike-swap.title: Strike out, swap the claim
strike-swap.use: Correct a common misconception: the old claim gets crossed out, the new one slams in.
strike-swap.avoid: Keep the old claim short (≤6 characters) so the strike lands in one stroke.
strike-swap.sfx: Strike = paper rustle (`sword`/`paper`) · new word = stamp/thud (`stamp`)

left-stair.title: Left-aligned stair
left-stair.use: Three-step progression: cause → process → result. Each line indents further and the previous line dims.
left-stair.avoid: More than 3 lines; keep each line short and put the keyword in big type.
left-stair.sfx: One ding per line, a heavier hit on the last line

a-to-b.title: A → B (cause and effect)
a-to-b.use: "The more A, the more B" / "because A, therefore B" — one arrow joins before and after.
a-to-b.avoid: A and B ≤ 4 characters each, or the arrow has no room.
a-to-b.sfx: A soft · arrow whoosh · B thud (`dong2`)

two-column.title: Two-column compare
two-column.use: Two options side by side. The centre line draws first, then one block on each side.
two-column.avoid: Wildly uneven text lengths look lopsided; keep each column ≤ 3 lines.
two-column.sfx: Centre line whoosh · one ding per side

bars.title: Highlighter bars
bars.use: Two parallel points, like a highlighter swipe (selling points, results).
bars.avoid: Keep bar text to 2–5 characters; more than 2 bars steals focus from the face.
bars.sfx: One ding or cash-register per bar (`cash`, `gold`)

vertical-wall.title: Right-wall vertical text
vertical-wall.use: A 2–4 character key word stacked on the right edge. Keeps the face clear — good for emotion/conclusion words.
vertical-wall.avoid: More than 4 characters; if the face sits on the right, mirror it to the left wall.
vertical-wall.sfx: One hit per character, heaviest on the last

dark-question.title: Dim + big question
dark-question.use: Low voice, rhetorical question, suspense. Edges darken, only one question stays, the camera creeps in.
dark-question.avoid: Max 1–2 per video, or it loses weight.
dark-question.sfx: A puzzled sound (`huh`) — or total silence

chapter.title: Chapter list 01/02
chapter.use: Explaining a method or steps: big number + title + ticked cards, with the picture lifted so text sits on the chest.
chapter.avoid: One number at a time; ≤ 2 cards.

giant-fill.title: Giant-character fill
giant-fill.use: The punchline: one huge hollow character above the head fills from the bottom as you say the key line.
giant-fill.avoid: One character only; at most once per video — save it for the last line.

typed-quote.title: Round window + typed quote
typed-quote.use: A quote/golden line: black background, a round portrait window on top, your words typed out character by character below.
typed-quote.avoid: Each line ≤ 9 characters; each character must appear when you actually say it.

signature.title: Signature card
signature.use: Outro: name + one-line persona + series name. Dimmed base, no heavy SFX, a clean ending.
signature.avoid: No more than 3 lines; no new information.

split-retention.title: Card over face · retention curve
split-retention.use: Hook / talking about "nobody watches to the end": a curve card draws on top, your portrait window below. Give viewers a visual hook in the first 3 seconds — not just captions.
split-retention.avoid: Don't put paragraphs in the card — one graphic plus one word; max 2 per video.
split-retention.sfx: Whoosh → tech-reveal → sigh (on the "swipe away" beat)

split-compare.title: Card over face · compare timelines
split-compare.use: "Messy vs tidy", "beginner vs pro": two small graphics side by side (✗ / ✓) on top, you talking below.
split-compare.avoid: The two sides must look clearly different (messy vs tidy) or the contrast is lost.

phone-swipe.title: Phone swipe-away
phone-swipe.use: Talking about viewers swiping away: your video plays inside a phone on black, three lines on the right build up, and on the key line the phone flicks upward.
phone-swipe.avoid: Max three lines of ≤ 6 characters (only ~360px of width on the right); don't chain it right after left-stair.

reporter.title: Reporter stand-up (cut-out in front)
reporter.use: Steps/lists: black background, a chapter card on top, you cut out and standing in front. Needs per-frame matting (macOS: Apple Vision).
reporter.avoid: Don't use it without matting (the preview shows a stand-in); one number per card.

pip-broll.title: Full-screen B-roll + PIP face
pip-broll.use: When you name a concrete thing (product, place, animal…): B-roll fills the screen and you shrink to a white-ringed round window. Rotate the window top-right / top-left / bottom-centre; don't cover the subject.
pip-broll.avoid: B-roll with no clear subject looks empty; keep the window off the label tag; don't reuse the same corner 3 times.

split-broll.title: Face on top, B-roll below (split screen)
split-broll.use: Talk while showing something: you on top (face stays put), a B-roll strip below, named with a yellow label tag.
split-broll.avoid: No captions on the strip (captions stay on you, y ≤ 1230); give static images a slow push.

broll-bottom.title: Bottom slide-in B-roll strip
broll-bottom.use: You stay full-screen; B-roll slides up over the lower ~45%. The lightest way to insert B-roll — good for a noun that flashes by.
broll-bottom.avoid: The strip covers the chest band, so captions must move out of the way (above the strip, or hidden for the moment).
broll-bottom.sfx: Whoosh (slide in) → nothing (keep the sound clean)

poster-hero.title: Poster hero word + dim
poster-hero.use: A key noun / pain word: a full-screen poster or AI image dimmed 40% and one gold (benefit) or red (pain) word slams in, then slowly grows across the shot.
poster-hero.avoid: Only the 2–3 most important words per video; keep it ≤ 4 characters or the type gets too small.
poster-hero.sfx: Stamp (`stamp`/`peng`) → cinematic impact when it reaches full size

label-hero.title: Label + hero overlap
label-hero.use: A small label stacked onto a big word (like "GMV" pressed onto "20M") so a number or key term reads at a glance; optionally add a white-box red-text mini tag.
label-hero.avoid: Don't use the same colour for label and hero; keep the hero ≤ 4 characters or it shrinks too much.

spread-hero.title: Wide-tracked hero word
spread-hero.use: A 1–3 character hero word with tracking stretched across the full width, like a poster headline ("DON'T / GAMBLE"). Top line yellow, bottom line white or red.
spread-hero.avoid: More than 3 characters falls apart when spread; use only for the harshest line, 1–2 times per video.

ghost-word.title: Ghost word (giant translucent glyph)
ghost-word.use: A giant translucent word as background ("烦", "WHY", "100%") with a small line on top that names the topic.
ghost-word.avoid: Don't put it over the face (this library keeps it in the chest band); no more than 3 glyphs or it turns to mush.

quote-card.title: Quote card (dimmed + blurred)
quote-card.use: Background dims and blurs; a numbered white-box tag plus the quoted line with the key words in yellow; a small right-aligned source line. For data, quotes and findings.
quote-card.avoid: Max 2 quotes of ≤ 2 lines each; keep the source short; don't use it for subjective claims that have no source.

chapter-tag.title: Chapter tag
chapter-tag.use: A yellow rounded block (italic number) + arrow + dashed-outline title — marks "point 1", lighter than a giant number.
chapter-tag.avoid: One number at a time; pick either this or the Chapter list, don't stack them.

motion-fade.title: Fade in
motion-fade.use: The workhorse base: knowledge, narration, ordinary lines; never steals focus (110 uses in the source pack — #1).
motion-fade.avoid: Don't use it when you need emphasis; don't use it on every line.
motion-fade.sfx: Paper rustle / soft whoosh, or none

motion-slide-up.title: Slide up
motion-slide-up.use: Gentle entrances: titles, list items one by one — a small upward drift plus fade.
motion-slide-up.avoid: Many lines in the same direction look stiff.

motion-reveal-up.title: Reveal upward
motion-reveal-up.use: Wipes on from the bottom upward: definitions and conclusions, a little ceremony.

motion-curtain.title: Curtain open
motion-curtain.use: Opens from the centre outward: opening titles, chapter names; a knowledge / classical feel.

motion-grow.title: Grow
motion-grow.use: Numbers and key points: scale up from half size, a "growing in" feel.
motion-grow.avoid: Don't combine with Slam in the same line.

motion-grow-soft.title: Soft grow
motion-grow-soft.use: Subtle motion for caption-level emphasis (a 6% scale).
motion-grow-soft.avoid: Too weak when you need impact.

motion-shrink.title: Shrink in
motion-shrink.use: Emphasis and reversals: starts slightly large and settles — a "dropping in" feel (80 uses — #2).
motion-shrink.avoid: Not for long sentences (the scaling pushes them out of bounds).

motion-slam.title: Slam
motion-slam.use: The single heaviest word: lands from 3× size to 1× — must have a heavy hit.
motion-slam.avoid: Max 2–3 per video; without a heavy SFX it feels hollow.

motion-glow-blur.title: Glow blur
motion-glow-blur.use: Emotional, mystical, soft lines: blurred → sharp with a little bloom (106 uses across three variants).
motion-glow-blur.avoid: Too slow (0.7 s) for fast-paced words.

motion-blur-left.title: Blur-slide left
motion-blur-left.use: Topic changes and transition-feel lines: slides in from the right with motion blur.
motion-blur-left.avoid: Not for text sitting on the right side.

motion-rise-random.title: Random rise
motion-rise-random.use: Knowledge / book-type lines: each character floats up from a different height.

motion-wave-bounce.title: Wave bounce
motion-wave-bounce.use: Light, playful words: characters bounce in one after another like a wave.
motion-wave-bounce.avoid: Wrong tone for legal / financial / serious content.

motion-typewriter.title: Typewriter
motion-typewriter.use: Definitions, keywords, a "typing" feel; the safest pairing is a typing sound (68 uses).
motion-typewriter.avoid: Slow for long lines (0.075 s per character).

motion-develop.title: Develop (char by char)
motion-develop.use: Calm, literary lines: each character develops from blurry grey to sharp.

motion-leap.title: Leap in
motion-leap.use: Punchy short words: leaps up into place with a little overshoot.

motion-roll-in.title: Roll in
motion-roll-in.use: Numbers, money, deals: rolls up like a slot machine.

motion-tracking-in.title: Tracking in
motion-tracking-in.use: Titles and golden lines: characters gather from wide spacing into place — a "focusing" feel (52 uses across two variants).
motion-tracking-in.avoid: The effect is hard to see with fewer than 3 characters.

motion-echo.title: Echo
motion-echo.use: Shouts, strong emotion, "Attention!": the word pops and sends echo rings outward.
motion-echo.avoid: Once or twice per video; not for long lines.

theme-biz-gold-red.title: Business gold & red
theme-biz-gold-red.use: Law, finance, loans, property, education, business, cars, study-abroad — credible and crisp. Smiley Sans as the main font + gold #ffbf17 / deep red #b71c1c (52% of the industry clips). Entrances lean to fade / grow / shrink / glow-blur; SFX lean to whoosh and impact.
theme-biz-gold-red.avoid: Gold = benefit and red = pain within a layout; don't add a third accent colour.

theme-guofeng-cream.title: Classical cream
theme-guofeng-cream.use: Wellness, women's emotion / growth, psychology, relationships, yoga, custom homes — gentle and refined. Serif fonts + cream #fff589 / deep red. Entrances lean to fade / grow-soft / curtain / develop; SFX lean to paper and whoosh.
theme-guofeng-cream.avoid: The pack uses Classical / Jinling fonts (not bundled); this library falls back to Source Han Serif Heavy, so the refined feel is weaker.

theme-knowledge-yellow.title: Knowledge yellow
theme-knowledge-yellow.use: Paid knowledge, career, founder IP, business coaches, used cars, property agents, reading, tax — bright and practical. Douyin Meihao as the supporting font + bright yellow #fff589 / deep red. Entrances lean to shrink / fade / curtain / blur-left; SFX lean to swish, paper, typing.
theme-knowledge-yellow.avoid: The densest pacing (about 78 blocks/min and 54 SFX/min — medians for 15–60 s shorts); don't copy it to long videos.

emo-cry.title: Cry (emotion loading)
emo-cry.use: One word carries a negative emotion: the text starts white and red fills it from the bottom like liquid (about 0.7 s), tracking stretched across the width. For words like "breakdown", "pain", "crying".
emo-cry.avoid: 1–2 per video; not for long lines; red is the pain colour, so don't stack it on layouts that already use red as the accent.

emo-surprise.title: Surprise (wave)
emo-surprise.use: Surprise and sudden turns: two characters bob out of phase, each tilted about ±8°, looping about 1 s, in gold.
emo-surprise.avoid: Gets messy with more characters (2–3 is best); wrong tone for serious content.

emo-joy.title: Joy (text glow)
emo-joy.use: Joy, good news, success: pale-yellow text with radiating light rays pulsing in beat behind it, about 1 s per cycle.
emo-joy.avoid: The rays wash over what is behind; don't use it together with large B-roll; 1–2 per video.

emo-shout.title: Shout (megaphone)
emo-shout.use: Shouting, calling for help, "Attention!": two characters tilt outward, fade in, then sway gently while echoes ripple outward.
emo-shout.avoid: Short words of 2–3 characters only; the echo grows beyond the text, so leave room on both sides.

glass-hero.title: Glass text (translucent gradient)
glass-hero.use: One hero word as "glass text": a gold gradient, but the light/dark texture of the picture behind shows through it, like frosted glass. For opening titles, brand words, the one big word in a video.
glass-hero.avoid: The picture behind needs light/dark variation (wood grain, brick, curtains) — a flat dark wall barely shows the effect; it must not sit inside a wrapper with transform / opacity / filter (the blend stops working).

text-behind.title: Text behind the person (matte)
text-behind.use: Big text placed behind the person: background → text → matte PNG on top, so the person covers part of the text and the frame gains depth. Needs per-frame matting (macOS: Apple Vision).
text-behind.avoid: Don't use it without a matte; put the text inside the same camera container as the video (so it follows hand-shake / push-ins); a frame without a matte draws no text — better no text than text across the face; keep the window to ~3 s (per-frame matting is slow).

glass-behind.title: Glass text behind the person
glass-behind.use: Both together: a gold glass word behind the person, texture showing through, the person covering part of it. The most premium-looking big text.
glass-behind.avoid: The limits of Glass text and Text behind combined; at most once per video — save it for the opening or the one key line.

top-title.title: Persistent top title
top-title.use: A two-line series name pinned to the top for the whole video (white + accent colour): someone who scrolls in late still knows the topic. Appears at the start and stays until just before the end.
top-title.avoid: Only when there is room above the head; a big face (head top ≈ y230) covers it, so lower the picture or make headroom first. Keep it under 8 characters, not a sentence.

stack-list.title: Stacking list (older lines dim)
stack-list.use: For 2–3 points: lines appear one by one, the older ones dim when a new one lands, and a closing line drops on top as a big word.
stack-list.avoid: More than 3 lines (with the closing word) or 4 (without) overflows the chest band; keep each line ≤ 8 characters.
stack-list.sfx: A ding per line, a heavy hit on the closing word

end-cta.title: Ending action (pill + arrow)
end-cta.use: The ending tells them where to tap next: a blue pill button + an arrow pointing to the bottom-left. Almost every industry video ends this way.
end-cta.avoid: The wording comes from the user; if there is no account / contact, don't invent one. Don't stack it with the signature card (pick one, or pill above and signature below).
end-cta.sfx: One very light ding, no heavy sound effect

camera-punch.title: Opening punch-in
camera-punch.use: The first second of the video: the picture punches from 1.28× to 1.0× with a bounce and motion blur. The first beat of the hook, paired with a whoosh.
camera-punch.avoid: Once per video, at the start; keep the face centred and high, or the punch pushes it out of frame.

camera-shake.title: Impact shake
camera-shake.use: On the beat a key word slams down, the picture shakes and pops to 1.06×. Only the picture shakes, not the text.
camera-shake.avoid: At most 4–6 per video, each on a real hit; never back to back.

camera-tvoff.title: TV switch-off
camera-tvoff.use: For "the ads stop, the business stops" / "it all disappeared": the picture squashes to a line, then a dot, then black, held until the next sentence.
camera-tvoff.avoid: Always give `until`, or the black runs to the end; only for "gone / over" sentences.

camera-send.title: Shrink into a phone and fly away
camera-send.use: For "send this video to him" / "share": the whole picture shrinks into a phone, pauses, then flies to the top right.
camera-send.avoid: Use the dark starfield behind it, not white; at most once, for the share call to action.

camera-circle.title: Picture becomes a circle + circles around
camera-circle.use: For "the peers around you / your team / your customers": the speaker shrinks to a circular avatar and circles pop out around him, joined by lines. The textbook "draw what you say".
camera-circle.avoid: Tell it where the face is (`face`); at most 6 circles; don't combine with captions and big text at once.

white-flash.title: White flash
white-flash.use: On the hook beat, a scene change or an impact: the whole screen flashes white for 0.22 s. Often on the same frame as the punch-in and a big word.
white-flash.avoid: At most 3–4 per video; not on quiet sentences.

kinetic-line.title: Word-by-word pop
kinetic-line.use: One word per beat: the new word pops in big, the previous one shrinks and dims above it; the hot word is accent-coloured and bigger. Good for the opening punchline.
kinetic-line.avoid: ≤ 6 words a line; each word timed to when it is spoken; don't squeeze it into the chest band together with captions.
kinetic-line.sfx: Pop / hit on the hot word

counter-slam.title: Number counts up and slams
counter-slam.use: For concrete numbers (8 deals, 500k, 10 years): it counts from 0, slows down, then lands with a slam and a glow — far stronger than just showing the number.
counter-slam.avoid: 1–3 numbers per video; the number must be what he actually said; put the unit in the suffix.

stamp.title: Stamp text
stamp.use: For "all of them were X" / "closed" / "key point": the text is stamped down from 2.2× to 1× with a slight tilt.
stamp.avoid: ≤ 6 characters; red / accent, not the same colour as the big text; 1–2 per video.

chat-dm.title: Chat box send
chat-dm.use: For "DM me X" / "comment X": an input box slides up, types, sends, and an accent bubble flies up. Makes the call to action visible.
chat-dm.avoid: Use the keyword he actually says (≤ 6 characters); put it at the end; don't also stack the ending pill.

slot-row.title: Empty slots pop in
slot-row.use: For "at least 7 deals" / "ten places" / "the goal": N dashed slots pop in one by one underneath.
slot-row.avoid: N ≤ 10; keep it in the chest band (y≈1050); don't cover captions.

rapid-montage.title: Screenshot flash
rapid-montage.use: Real screenshots as evidence: each one punches in for 0.2 s with a slight tilt, the last one holds, "No. N" on top. A real screenshot beats any animation.
rapid-montage.avoid: Supply the screenshots yourself (under public, with their pixel sizes); blank out other people's names and phone numbers; at most 12.

jy-text-a.title: JianYing text animations A (4)
jy-text-a.use: 4 of the 24 JianYing presets: reveal up / random rise / blur glow / shout wave. Each preset's offset / scale / brightness / blur is written as a per-frame table measured from the JianYing sample; sound effects are paired automatically.
jy-text-a.avoid: Not every word needs to move (52% of the original pack's text has no animation); one preset per sentence, never the same one twice in a row.

jy-text-b.title: JianYing text animations B (4)
jy-text-b.use: Shrink II (big first, then slam) / wave bounce / typewriter / leap. The "bounce" presets overshoot and pair with variety-show sounds; the rest are basically ease-out.
jy-text-b.avoid: Bounce only for light words; typewriter only for definitions / keywords; don't make everything bounce.

backdrop-cosmos.title: Starfield backdrop page
backdrop-cosmos.use: The layer revealed when the person shrinks to an avatar or a phone: a dark starfield with three parallax layers and a slowly turning nine-grid; colours come from the theme. No images needed.
backdrop-cosmos.avoid: Don't use it as the whole-video background (it competes with the person); only for "black page" scenes.

particles.title: Gold dust / fireflies
particles.use: An ambient layer over the picture: gold = dust drifting up, firefly = warm fireflies that blink. Gives a traditional / story feel some air.
particles.avoid: Keep it sparse (n ≤ 60); not for fast-paced videos, it looks dirty.

ink-wipe.title: Ink-wash transition
ink-wipe.use: A transition between two segments: a blob of ink spreads from the centre to cover the screen, then recedes (blot / brush sweep / splash / rise). Traditional / story feel.
ink-wipe.avoid: At most 3 per video; 0.9 s long, don't put it over a key word.

zh.title: video-craft 版式库
zh.lede1: 给 Claude Code 用的口播剪辑 skill。这里是它会用到的
zh.lede2: 个文字版式、字搭配、文字动画、换场和抖音精剪画面——悬停预览，点开看什么时候用、什么时候别用、配什么音效。
zh.search: 搜索：划走、对比、金句、钩子…
zh.safe: 所有字都守安全区：x 60–1010、y 250–1250（y>900 时右边收到 950）。字幕最多两行、每行 ≤12 字。下面的预览用占位人形，不是真人。
zh.empty: 没有找到匹配的版式，换个词试试。
zh.cpPrompt: 复制给 AI 的指令
zh.toastPrompt: 已复制，粘贴给 Claude Code
lim: 预览是静态示例，动态手感（砸字力度、淡出时机）要自己看一遍。
「记者出镜」需要逐帧抠像，目前只有 macOS（Apple Vision）能跑。
音效和 BGM 不附带（版权），请自备可商用文件，按 id 命名。
精剪的素材（B-roll）是占位画面；真用时换成实拍 / stock / AI 图。
没有自动越界检测：靠渲染时自动缩小推回 + 安全区红框目视检查。
文字动画预览是循环播放的示例；只核对了动到一半的静帧，没有逐帧核对速度曲线。

sfx.title: 音效配对表
sfx.lede: 入场动画 → 最常配的音效。来自 66 个行业成片的统计（每个文字片段 ±0.5 秒内最近的音效，共 {n} 对）。
sfx.fact1: {pct}% 的音效和字在同一帧起声（{same}/{n}）——音效起点 = 字出现的第一帧，不提前、不延后。
sfx.fact2: 音量没有统一电平：{down} 个压低（中位 {dm}×≈−7 dB）、{up} 个拉高（中位 {um}×≈+6 dB）、其余默认。
sfx.search: 搜索动画或音效：缩小、打字、水滴…
sfx.note: 「本库 id」= references/sfx-pairing.md 里的语义 id；— = 本库没有收这个音效。音效文件不随仓库发布。

en.title: video-craft layout library
en.lede1: A talking-head editing skill for Claude Code. These are the
en.lede2: text layouts, typography pairings, text-motion presets, scene changes and Douyin-style (精剪) cuts it uses — hover to preview, click for when to use it, when not to, and which sound effect to pair.
en.safe: Every piece of text respects the safe zone: x 60–1010, y 250–1250 (right edge pulled in to 950 below y 900). Captions: max two lines, ≤12 characters each. Previews use a placeholder figure, not a real person.
en.empty: No matching layout — try another word.
lim: Previews are static examples — watch the motion yourself (hit strength, fade timing).
"Reporter stand-up" needs per-frame matting; currently only macOS (Apple Vision) can run it.
SFX and BGM are not included (licensing). Bring your own commercially usable files, named by id.
B-roll in the Douyin-style cuts is a placeholder; swap in real footage / stock / AI images.
No automatic out-of-bounds detection: relies on shrink-and-nudge at render time plus visual checks with the safe-zone guides.
Text-motion previews are looping examples; only mid-animation stills were checked — easing curves were not verified frame by frame.

sfx.title: SFX pairing table
sfx.lede: Entrance animation → the SFX it is most often paired with. Statistics from 66 industry clips (the nearest SFX within ±0.5 s of each text segment, {n} pairs).
sfx.fact1: {pct}% of SFX start on the same frame as the text ({same}/{n}) — the SFX starts on the first frame the text appears, no earlier, no later.
sfx.fact2: There is no single level: {down} lowered (median {dm}× ≈ −7 dB), {up} raised (median {um}× ≈ +6 dB), the rest at default.
sfx.search: Search an animation or sound: shrink, typing, water drop…
sfx.note: "Library id" = the semantic id in references/sfx-pairing.md; — = this library does not include that sound. SFX files are not distributed with the repo.
